question.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ where $n$ is the number of trials, and $p$ is the probability of success on each trial,  we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(5,\frac{1}{3}),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{x}){(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}{(\frac{2}{3})}^{5-x}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1\le X\le 2) & =P(X\in \{1,2\}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}){(\frac{1}{3})}^{1}{(\frac{2}{3})}^{5-1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}){(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}{(\frac{2}{3})}^{5-2} \\  & =5{(\frac{1}{3})}^{1}{(\frac{2}{3})}^{4}+10{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}{(\frac{2}{3})}^{3} \\  & =\frac{160}{243}.\end{aligned}
$$
